description: DB integration: after the migration, a client-visible document is requester, a non-visible one is organization_private, a non-visible one created by a seat-assigned user is shared_it, and is_client_visible equals audience = 'requester' on documents and folders
DB integration: the migration applies on the Citus regression container with documents distributed, and a direct write to is_client_visible is refused
Unit: the content-audience predicate gives the PRD's reader table for staff, seat and requester, and the comment callers return what they returned before the rename

DB integration: a seat technician uploads to a task of a shared project and to an in-scope ticket; the author and a second seat technician of the same client list and load both by document id and by file id; MSP staff read them; a portal user does not

DB integration: an MSP staff upload on an in-scope ticket with the default audience is absent from the seat technician's list, counts and folder tree, and refused by getDocument, preview, download and the file-id routes

DB integration: MSP staff move a document through organization_private, shared_it and requester; seat and portal visibility follow at each step; a seat technician and a portal user calling the setter are refused
DB integration: a seat technician cannot store organization_private by explicit choice, by uploading into an organization_private folder, or through the REST write
DB integration: a shared_it document attached to a task of an unshared project, or to a ticket on an out-of-scope board, is refused to the seat technician for read and for create
Contract: for every resource in the seat policy, each condition on read is also a condition on create
Unit: shared_audience and attached_parents_in_scope agree between their JS and SQL facets over a table of records, including a record with no attached parent and one missing the attribute
DB integration: a document attached to a comment the seat cannot read stays hidden from the seat although its own audience is requester
CE: with EDITION=community, every writer refuses shared_it, the two-state control writes organization_private and requester, and document upload, list and portal read work for a plain tenant
API: a write with only is_client_visible maps to requester or the author's default; a write with conflicting is_client_visible and audience is rejected; reads return both fields
Component: a tenant with a seat arrangement gets three audiences for MSP staff and two for a seat technician in the upload dialog

Component: a Pro tenant holding the co-managed capability with no seat arrangement renders the document row, drawer, upload dialog, folder control and list indicator as they render before this change, with no Shared with client IT option anywhere
